RagShortTexts: Fur trading distinguishes species, season and damage.
Bundled pelts still require counting and quality inspection.

Variants.Content: Fur buyers examine coat, condition, season and dry keeping. Bundles ease transport but conceal inferior pelts. Inspection and agreement on payment by skin or bundle reduce mixing, shortages and disputes.
Fur escorts guard against damp and loose bundles. Counting at both warehouse handovers locates losses better than relying on an outer mark.
Buyers and collectors specify acceptable quality. Equal counting of damaged and sound pelts provokes disputes; nominal numbers are not realized value.
Hunters prepare and store pelts before sale. Inspection delays a bargain but avoids chasing compensation after damaged goods have traveled away.
